name: Apteva Apps
description: Curated registry of Apteva Apps. Each entry points at a manifest URL the platform can fetch + install.

apps.name: stocks
apps.description: Explore + screen the S&P 1500 (every Dividend Aristocrat & King) backed by Yahoo Finance. Min/max filters on market cap, dividend yield, payout ratio, P/E, and 5-year dividend growth; smart watchlists (rule-driven, manual, or hybrid) with live membership; per-stock quote, price chart, dividend history. Read-only: never places orders, holds no ledger. Free Yahoo public endpoints, no API key.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: simple
apps.description: Minimal read-only UI for watching an Apteva agent — embed anywhere on the same host. Same-origin, path-mounted SPA; no sidecar.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: demo
apps.description: Client-facing demo runner. State board with live MCP-polled scenario cards, control rail with seed/reset recipes + scripted scenario triggers, chat dock for natural-language Q&A with the agent. Designed as a kiosk surface for client meetings.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: tasks
apps.description: Mission board for an Apteva agent. Agents create and complete tasks via MCP tools; the dashboard tracks progress live. Tasks can be created in 'planning' mode for the agent to draft a proposal first.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: todo
apps.description: Personal todo list — human-first counterpart to the agent mission board. Inbox / Today / Upcoming, lists (user-facing buckets), tags (cross-cutting context), priorities, due dates, snooze, and recurrence. Agent helps via natural-language quick-add, list, snooze, and complete tools.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: health
apps.description: Personal health log — weight, sleep, mood, heart rate, blood pressure, workouts. One flexible time-series table for any numeric metric plus a workouts list. Agent ingests natural-language one-liners ('weight 78.4', 'ran 5k 26min', 'bp 122/78') via health_log; the panel charts pinned kinds and lists recent sessions. v0.2 will add device sync (Apple Health, Oura, Garmin).
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: status
apps.description: Per-agent status line. Agent writes 'what I'm on right now' via MCP; dashboard reads it live. Short-horizon counterpart to the long-lived directive. Includes a panel for operators to view, set, and clear the line, plus a /status skill teaching the cadence + tone protocol.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: crm
apps.description: Contacts store for Apteva agents and human teams. Multi-value channels, typed custom attributes with provenance, append-only activity log, soft-delete + merge.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: computer
apps.description: Watch and steer browser sessions through the generic browser_session and computer_use MCP tools. v0.7.6 adds app-owned provider settings so Browserbase, Steel, local Chrome, Browser Engine, or service can be selected as the default provider and optionally enforced for agents, while retaining the enlarged stable viewport, fixed click coordinates, app-managed contexts, save/open/restore panel controls, provider live links, and direct computer_use interactions.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: screenshots
apps.description: Capture browser screenshots from a URL, save them to storage, and browse them in a gallery. Built on the `computer` app for the browser session and `storage` for the bytes — this app owns no browser plumbing itself. Four MCP tools (capture / list / get / delete) plus a gallery panel and a chat-attachable screenshot-card the agent posts after a successful capture. Idempotency_key on capture deduplicates retries within a 10-minute window. v0.1 supports URL-driven capture only; attaching to a session the agent already opened lands when computer exposes session resume.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: storage
apps.description: File storage with virtual folders, signed URLs, dedup. Pluggable backend: local disk by default, S3-compatible (AWS / R2 / B2 / Wasabi / MinIO) when configured. On S3, presigned upload + download URLs let clients transfer bytes directly to the bucket — bytes never proxy through this container. v0.9.5 adds files_get_content for inline byte fetch via CallAppResult — fixes the multi-storage-install case where signed URLs route to the wrong instance.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: tables
apps.description: Typed-row database for Apteva agents and human teams. The row-shaped sibling to storage: define typed tables (text, number, bool, datetime, json, file_id), insert rows with strict validation, query with typed predicates, paginate. Read-only SELECT escape hatch with {table_name} placeholders for aggregations the named tools can't express. Project-scoped by default; opt-in global tables for shared lookup data.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: jobs
apps.description: Scheduled-job runner. Other apps (and agents) enqueue work to be delivered later — once at a future time, on an interval, or on a cron expression. At-least-once delivery with idempotency keys, exponential backoff, and a runs log.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: functions
apps.description: Lambda-style serverless functions in node or Go. Each function is an immutable, built version served by a pool of warm worker processes — the runtime boots once and serves invocations over a socketpair, no per-request spawn. Handlers reach other Apteva apps via context.call. Deploy-time build (npm install / go build), immutable versions with rollback, auto-routed HTTP at /fn/<name>.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: workflows
apps.description: Deterministic, on-demand pipelines. A workflow is a YAML/JSON graph of typed steps (http, function, app, integration, emit, branch) with goto-style branching and per-step retry. Triggered by HTTP, manual invocation, or another app's events (the sidecar opens one multiplexed SSE subscription per (source, project) lane); integration steps reach any in-project connection (Pushover, Slack, Resend, ...) by id without operator pre-binding. Per-step audit log so every run is inspectable, retryable, replayable. Strict separation from agents: workflows never call LLMs — if a step needs judgment it sends an event to an agent and the workflow ends.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: code
apps.description: Repositories — named, framework-tagged code workspaces scoped under Apteva projects. First-class editing tools modelled on Claude Code: partial reads with line numbers, exact-match string edits with uniqueness checks, atomic multi-edit, repo-wide grep + glob.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: simulator
apps.description: iOS and Android simulators on demand. Boot a device, build a repo's source into an APK/.app, install + launch on a headless emulator or Simulator, stream the screen to the browser, and relay touch + key input. Called by Apteva Code on Run for mobile repos; usable standalone for any flow that produces a mobile artifact.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: media
apps.description: Catalog + derivations + renders + transcripts + auto-descriptions for audio/video/image files in storage. Pluggable render backend: ffmpeg by default, Cloudinary when bound (offload trim/resize/transcode/crop/extract_frame). Subscribes to storage events for instant indexing on upload + cascade cleanup on delete; falls back to a 30s safety-net poll. Smart video thumbnails skip black/fade openings.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: media-studio
apps.description: Generate or edit images, video, and talking-head avatar videos via any compatible provider. media_generate(kind, prompt, …) — image / video / audio / music / avatar. source_image switches images into edit and video into image-to-video; kind=avatar makes a replica/avatar speak a script (Tavus or HeyGen). Async kinds queue + poll automatically. Today: OpenAI + Venice for image; Venice for image edit + text/image-to-video; Tavus + HeyGen for avatars. Live-loaded model + constraint-aware composer with avatar/voice pickers. Optionally saves outputs to the Storage app.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: composer
apps.description: Multi-clip video composition. Stitch generated or uploaded assets into a single video — clips on a track, optional soundtrack, text overlays. v0.1 renders locally via the sidecar's bundled ffmpeg or on a render host via instances. v0.2 adds SaaS render backends (Shotstack et al) via the render_executor integration role.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: calendar
apps.description: Self-contained calendar — multiple calendars per project, events with recurrence (rrule), holidays helper. Agents read + write via MCP tools; the panel renders day / week / month / year / agenda views with click-to-create and drag-to-move. Multi-day + all-day events render clearly across views: truly continuous spanning bars in month view (per-week overlay), a dedicated all-day strip above the week/day timed grid, and connected span bars in the larger year mini-calendars.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: trips
apps.description: Plan trips end-to-end: destinations, transport, accommodation, activities, packing list, budget. Calendar sync keeps trip, transport, stay, and activity events in step as items are added, moved, or removed. Optional Duffel and Google Places integrations power search; flight searches feed long-lived price intelligence, global deal scans, airport autocomplete, and route/date heatmaps.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: social
apps.description: Schedule and publish posts to your social media accounts (X, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Pinterest, Threads). Connect accounts from inside the app — no separate integration setup. Posts can be triggered from the panel or by an agent via MCP tools.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: messaging
apps.description: Send and receive messages across channels (email via SES, SMS+WhatsApp via Twilio). Tracks SES/SNS delivery events including delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complaints, delays, rejects, and rendering failures; mirrors them into Apteva message events and the operator panel. Sender setup can be rechecked idempotently to refresh SES identity, DNS, inbound receiving, SNS notifications, and delivery event wiring.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: email-checker
apps.description: Stateless email validation — no DB, every call resolves fresh. email_check returns RFC 5322 syntax, DNS MX records, and list-based classification (disposable provider, free provider, role account) with a combined valid verdict. email_check_smtp runs an EHLO + MAIL FROM <> + RCPT TO probe against the domain's MX, flagging informative=false for Google/Microsoft (which accept every RCPT) and for blocked or greylisted responses. Also exposes a REST mirror at /check?email=.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: domains
apps.description: DNS + domain inventory for Apteva projects. Other apps (messaging for SES MX/DKIM, storage for CDN CNAMEs) call this app for DNS record CRUD instead of speaking each registrar's API directly. v0.2 ships the full operator panel (add/remove domains, browse + add/edit/delete records inline) and Namecheap support via per-slug provider dispatch (XML response parsing + read-modify-write semantics). Porkbun and Namecheap both work end-to-end.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: deploy
apps.description: Local-first builds and runtime supervision for Apteva projects. Pluggable source kinds (code, local) and frameworks (go, static, blank) — fetches source, runs the framework toolchain, supervises the result as a child process bound to a local port. No Docker required for v0.1; future runtimes (Docker, SSH-to-VPS) plug in behind the same Runtime interface.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: channel-chat
apps.description: Chat bridge between the agent and the dashboard / external channels. Persists messages with monotonic ids for clean reconnect. Currently bundled with apteva-server as a built-in framework app; will be extracted to a standalone installable app in a future release.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: trading
apps.description: Trading desk for Apteva agents. Multi-portfolio, multi-asset (equity, crypto, polymarket). Each portfolio runs in paper mode (deterministic in-process engine) or live mode (orders route through a bound broker integration; v0.2 ships Binance only). Mandate, allowed asset classes, and daily-loss halt enforced server-side; halt cancels working broker orders upstream. Approval policy lives in the agent's directive, not the platform.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: torrent
apps.description: BitTorrent client + indexer-search frontend. Search across configured Jackett / Prowlarr / RSS sources, add downloads by magnet or .torrent URL; on completion the resulting files are uploaded to the storage app and probed by media. Generic — ships with no indexers preconfigured; the user supplies sources and is responsible for what they download.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: dlna
apps.description: Publishes a UPnP/DLNA MediaServer on the LAN. Smart TVs, game consoles, Sonos, VLC, and other AV clients discover the server via SSDP and browse a virtual library backed by the storage app for bytes + folder structure, and the media app for duration / codec / resolution metadata. No transcoding in v0.1: clients that can't decode the source codec see the file in the listing but won't play it.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: backup
apps.description: Periodic backups of your Apteva instance — server DB plus every installed app's data. Captured via the platform snapshot endpoint (online, consistent, non-blocking) and shipped to a destination of your choice: local disk for self-hosters, or any S3-compatible bucket (AWS, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO). Schedules are driven by the jobs app so cron behaviour, retries, and run history all live in one familiar place. Restores stream back through /api/platform/restore — app DBs are swapped live; the platform DB is staged and applied on the next server boot.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: live-link
apps.description: Public HTTPS URL for a locally-installed Apteva instance. Two modes: quick (default) spawns a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel for an anonymous trycloudflare.com URL on every start — zero config, no account; named uses a Cloudflare API token + account/zone IDs to give a stable URL on a hostname you own (e.g. tunnel.example.com), creating-or-adopting a cfd_tunnel, configuring its ingress via the API, and upserting a proxied CNAME — restarts reuse the same URL. Surfaces in the project page with copy/stop/destroy controls and a runs history tagged by mode. Four MCP tools (expose_start/stop/status/destroy) let agents drive both modes. Auto-installs cloudflared on first use for linux/{amd64,arm64,arm,386} and darwin/{amd64,arm64}; falls back to PATH or a config-pinned binary on other hosts. ngrok, tailscale-funnel, and PUBLIC_URL auto-rewrite arrive in v0.3+.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: billing
apps.description: Customers, invoices, and payments — the AR core. Issuer settings (your legal entity) + EU reverse-charge auto-detection + country-name rendering on the PDF. Stripe enters as the `payment_processor` integration role (v0.8.0+): bind a Stripe connection once and agents call invoices_send_payment_link(invoice_id) to share a Stripe Checkout URL with the customer. The /webhooks/stripe endpoint verifies the signature via the integration's process_webhook tool and records payments idempotently on the (method, external_id) unique index. When no Stripe is bound, degrades cleanly to manual wire / cash / check / other recording. Catalog optional dep: invoice line items can reference a catalog price_id to snapshot description + unit_price, with FKs preserved for revenue-by-product analytics. Lifecycle: draft → open → paid / void / uncollectible. PDF + HTML print views render from line item snapshots so historical invoices stay stable even when catalog prices change. SQLite-backed; one currency per invoice; tax in basis points.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: catalog
apps.description: Products and prices — the source-of-truth app for what your business sells. Modelled after Stripe's Product + Price split: one product, many prices (different currencies, intervals, tiers). Lower-layer commerce app — catalog calls nothing; downstream apps (billing, future subscriptions/checkout) call here. Prices are effectively immutable for financial fields after create (unit_amount_cents, currency, interval) — to change pricing, create a new price and archive the old one. Same rule Stripe enforces. Soft-delete only so invoice/subscription references always resolve. 11 MCP tools across products + prices CRUD. Two-column panel with list + detail and 4 form modals (Create/Edit Product, Create/Edit Price). Chat-attachable product-card and price-card components. Forward-compat Stripe mirroring columns (external_id) on both tables — populated when billing's Stripe integration mirror lands.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: checkout
apps.description: Cart + buy flow — the orchestrator that turns a customer's intent into a real billing invoice. Three tables (carts, cart_items, checkout_sessions) implement the full state machine: open → checkout (locked while a session is awaiting payment) → converted (terminal, linked to billing invoice) or abandoned (TTL). Sits between content (storefront rendering) and billing (order ledger). Cart items snapshot from catalog prices at add-time so totals stay stable even if catalog pricing changes mid-session. On pay, calls billing.customers_upsert_by_email + invoices_create + invoices_finalize to mint a real invoice (idempotent + auditable). v0.1.0 ships the manual-payment path — agent/customer records the wire transfer in billing once received. v0.2.0 adds Stripe Checkout Session via the same payment_processor integration billing uses, with webhook-driven auto-paid flow. 9 MCP tools across cart_* and checkout_*. Admin panel with Carts + Sessions tabs.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: bills
apps.description: Vendors, bills, and outbound payments — the AP mirror of billing. Lifecycle (received → approved → scheduled → paid) plus disputed / void. Per-bill provider field stays local in v0.1.x; bank-rail providers (Mercury / Wise / Bill.com) land in v0.2. PDF voucher rendering for filing/audit. Drop a PDF on the bills tab and it's uploaded straight away — bind OpenCode Go (Kimi K2.6 default, vision-capable) in the Bindings tab and OCR auto-fills vendor + line items + dates + totals automatically (binding IS the on switch as of v0.1.5; no separate config flip required). Caller args always win. PDF rendering via embedded PDFium-WASM (no CGO, no system deps). Storage app is a declared dep so it auto-installs.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: finance
apps.description: Unified personal-wealth tracker — cash, brokerage positions, P2P loans, crypto, real estate, vehicles, pensions, loans, all in one ledger. Three nouns model everything: accounts (a place that holds value), instruments (the thing held — AAPL, BTC, EUR, your house), holdings (account × instrument → quantity + cost basis). Money in signed integer minor units; avg-cost accounting with cost_basis_delta on every txn so realised P&L is one column sum. Convenience tools for buy/sell/dividend/interest/transfer/valuation. Reports: net worth (point or monthly series, by account/kind/currency), allocation, performance (realised + unrealised P&L), cashflow (income vs expense per period). Per-category monthly budgets with hierarchical rollup. CSV import. v0.1 is manual entry; v0.2 plugs in integrations (Trading 212 first, then Plaid / Mintos / Binance) via the platform integrations engine — manual and integrated rows are indistinguishable downstream.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: mqtt
apps.description: Embedded MQTT broker for Apteva. Acts as the LAN message bus for smart-home devices (ESP32, Zigbee2MQTT, Tasmota, anything that speaks MQTT 3.1.1 or 5.0). Every published message is mirrored onto the platform event bus as `mqtt.message` so sibling apps (messaging, jobs, calendar) can react without speaking MQTT themselves; per-pattern subscriptions promote interesting topics to named bus events. Auto-discovers Home Assistant-convention devices by parsing `homeassistant/+/+/config`. Username/password auth + per-user topic ACL; an `apteva-default` user is seeded with a random password on first install (logged once).
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: tapo
apps.description: Local-LAN control of TP-Link Tapo cameras. Pan/tilt/zoom, snapshots, RTSP stream URLs, motion events, privacy + LED + night-mode toggles, presets. Talks the camera's HTTPS JSON-RPC directly with the secure_passthrough auth flow shipped on every internet-connected Tapo camera since TP-Link's Sept-2023 security patch. No cloud round-trips; everything goes peer-to-peer over the LAN. Setup requires enabling Third-Party Compatibility in the Tapo app (Me → Tapo Lab) on app version >= 3.8.103.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: ffmpeg
apps.description: Stateless ffmpeg-as-a-service for sibling Apteva apps. Three sync MCP tools — ffmpeg_grab_frame, ffmpeg_probe, ffmpeg_version — that wrap the local ffmpeg/ffprobe binaries. tapo's snapshot_capture is the v0.1 use case: grab one frame from a camera's RTSP stream without forcing every camera-y app to bundle its own ffmpeg. No DB, no panel, no async tools — minimal shape. Requires ffmpeg + ffprobe on PATH; OnMount refuses to start with a clear 'install ffmpeg' error if either is missing.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: docs
apps.description: Generate client-facing PDFs from markdown templates and store them in storage. Pure-Go render pipeline (no Chromium): markdown body + Go-template placeholders, rendered via maroto. Audit trail on every render — who rendered what template with which data — for compliance use cases (invoices, contracts, NDAs). Past renders keep working even after a template is edited because the output is a stable storage file_id.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: instances
apps.description: Compute-host inventory + lifecycle for Apteva. Manages the local Apteva machine and remote VPS instances under one MCP/REST surface so other apps (Live Link self-vps, Deploy SSHRuntime, Backup off-host, future Containers/Database/MQTT/game-server apps) bind a single "compute" dependency instead of each speaking VPS-provider APIs directly. The local machine is auto-seeded as instance id=0 and is always 'ready' — cannot be created or destroyed via the public API. Remote instances in v0.1 are provisioned via Hetzner Cloud (DigitalOcean / Vultr / AWS EC2 in v0.2). Per-instance Ed25519 SSH keypair seeded into the box via cloud-init authorized_keys; background readiness probe flips status='provisioning' → 'ready' once SSH accepts the key. Eight MCP tools: instance_create / _get / _list / _destroy / _run_command / _upload_file / _wait_ready / _metrics. Vitals (CPU / mem / disk / net / load / uptime) via gopsutil locally and a /proc-parsing bash script over SSH remotely, cached 5s per host.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: fleet
apps.description: Control plane for a fleet of client apteva instances. Spawns each tenant as a local apteva process on the parent host with its own data dir and port, supervised by fleet. Admin-driven bootstrap: tenant_create mints a setup token + returns the setup URL; the operator finishes admin registration in the browser and pastes the resulting api_key back via tenant_attach_key. Encrypted api_key keyring (AES-GCM, master key from FLEET_MASTER_KEY env or auto-generated on first boot). Nine MCP tools: tenant_create / _attach_key / _connect / _list / _get / _start / _stop / _delete / _support_login / _run_remote. Health poller every 60s with 5-failure disconnect threshold; boot reconciler reattaches surviving children after parent restart. Zero cross-app deps. Forward-compatible kind enum (local / remote today; docker / vps coming) means future provisioners drop in without breaking the registry.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: robot
apps.description: Agent navigation eval sandbox. 2D grid worlds the agent perceives partially (radius=2 default) and moves through one cardinal cell at a time. Episodes terminate via the harness — success on goal-reach or timeout at max_steps; the agent has no quit tool. A* baseline computed at scenario load powers an optimality_ratio metric on every successful run. Five gameplay tools (observe / move / pick / drop / no-give-up) plus three control tools (list_scenarios / start_episode / episode_status). pick + drop are reserved in the contract for v0.2 items. Three starter scenarios: empty_room, corridor (S-shape), warehouse_01 (three shelves).
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: vpn
apps.description: Backend-agnostic VPN orchestrator. Provisions a VPN server on an Instances host (local id 0 or a Hetzner VPS), generates keys, uploads daemon config, brings the interface up, and polls peer statistics on a timer. v0.1 ships WireGuard with native client support on macOS, iOS, Windows, Android, and Linux — the .conf returned by vpn_peer_add imports unchanged into every platform's official WG app. The internal Backend interface accommodates OpenVPN / IKEv2 later without changes to the MCP tool surface; tool names are protocol-neutral (vpn_peer_add, not wg_peer_add). Peers are created and revoked exclusively via MCP tools; the panel is monitor-only.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: certs
apps.description: TLS certificate issuance for Apteva projects via Let's Encrypt (or any RFC 8555 ACME directory). Two challenge types: DNS-01 routes TXT writes through the Domains app (no registrar credentials held here); HTTP-01 uses the webroot pattern (writes /.well-known/acme-challenge/<token> to a directory served by whatever reverse proxy is on :80 — Caddy, nginx, traefik). Async issuance, daily renewal worker, privileged cert_material tool gated to the server's TLS cache.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: routes
apps.description: Hostname-based routing for Apteva — owns the table mapping public hostnames (blog.example.com) to local backend targets (http://127.0.0.1:7100). Apps register routes via routes_register; apteva-server reads the table and reverse-proxies inbound traffic. Optional: uninstall and the platform falls back to path-based routing. Works the same for cloud installs (browser → public IP → apteva-server) and tunnel installs (cloudflared etc).
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: cdn
apps.description: Public-facing edge for apps that emit URLs. Composes Domains (DNS), Certs (TLS), and Routes (host-based reverse-proxy) into one capability: given an origin and a hostname, expose it publicly. The CDN panel can now create managed hostnames by picking a Domains inventory domain plus subdomain, and app origins by selecting a running project/global app. Origin can still be a static URL or an installed app by name (origin_app / cdn_link_app) — apteva-server resolves the app's live sidecar per request, so the zone survives restarts. apteva-server fronts it with an in-process edge cache for public assets (honors Cache-Control/ETag). Domains and Certs are optional (skip_dns / allow_http). Consumers (storage today, media-studio and podcast later) call cdn_url_for to mint URLs on a linked zone.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: redirects
apps.description: Branded short links and domain redirects. Each rule maps a (hostname, path) pair to an external URL and answers with a 301/302/307/308 + Location header. Think Bitly on your own domain, or EasyRedir for post-rebrand migrations. Composes on top of Routes (claims the public hostname so apteva-server reverse-proxies inbound traffic here) and optionally Domains (upserts a CNAME pointing at the platform when the apex is managed there). Match modes: exact and prefix (longest wins, segment-boundary safe); preserve_path forwards the leftover path on prefix rules, preserve_query merges inbound query strings.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: affiliate
apps.description: Publisher-side affiliate manager. Connect affiliate networks, refresh offers and performance stats, create monetized links, and optionally wrap them with branded redirects. Normalizes networks, offers, links, and daily stats across Target Circle/Circlewise, Impact, Awin, CJ Affiliate, Amazon Associates, Skimlinks, Sovrn, PartnerStack, and ShareASale integrations.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: content
apps.description: Multi-site block-based CMS. One project hosts 1..N sites — each with its own posts, pages, terms, menus, settings, theme, and optional hostname. Per-site templates (Finance Blog, SaaS Marketing, Docs Site bundled). Posts and pages with hierarchy, media, taxonomies, menus, revisions, redirects. Canonical body is a JSON block tree; 16 core block types shipped. Dashboard panel includes a Content tab (list + block editor), Templates tab (one-click site scaffolds), and a site switcher that auto-hides on single-site installs. Renders themed HTML at /, /posts/:slug, /:nested-page, term archives, feed.xml, and sitemap.xml; host-based dispatch routes domain-linked traffic to the right site automatically. Same data exposed as REST under /api/apps/content/admin/* so external frontends share the database without touching the theme path.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: gigs
apps.description: Agents delegate atomic work to human workers (CRM contacts) by composing reusable multi-modal instructions — text, audio, video, images, documents, checklists, confirmations, and the full input_* family. Templates are saved instruction sets; gigs are dispatched snapshots whose result schema, media manifest, and checklist are derived from the composition (never hand-authored). Workers receive a magic-link page via crm.contacts_send_message, read/watch the instructions, fill the form, upload attachments through storage, and submit. Yes/no and short-text gigs also accept thread replies via the CRM conversation. workers_create upserts a CRM contact and promotes it to a worker in one MCP call. CRM and storage are required dependencies; messaging is reached indirectly through CRM.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: auth
apps.description: Identity layer for Apteva-deployed SaaS: email + password signup/login, EdDSA JWT issuance with JWKS, refresh-token rotation, OAuth client registry (one user pool, many clients), email verification, password reset, magic links, and TOTP MFA. Agents administer the user pool via MCP tools; the deployed frontend hits the public HTTP routes; the dashboard renders a consolidated Auth panel (Overview / Users / Clients / Endpoints). Messaging is an optional dependency for transactional email.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: market-intel
apps.description: Cross-source market-intelligence gateway for trading agents. Ask in domain language ("Alcaraz clay H2H", "current Fed-cut probability", "enrich this Polymarket market") and market-intel fans out to the right bound data sources — prediction markets, sportsbook odds, macro, news, crypto — normalizes, de-vigs, and returns one consistent result. Read-only: it reads prices/stats/history; the agent decides; the trading app executes. v0.1 ships the unified query gateway; the background signal engine (arbitrage detection + events) lands in v0.2.
apps.author: Apteva

apps.name: analytics
apps.description: Generic event analytics for Apteva apps. Three ingest paths: (1) bus auto-capture — opt-in, records what every app already emits on the platform event bus, so no app needs a dependency on analytics; (2) analytics_track — explicit/typed events from apps that want them; (3) a static-site tag (public write key + hosted tag.js + GET /collect) for any website, like a classic analytics snippet. analytics_query / count / top / topics surface aggregates over JSON props. The dashboard panel is real-time (overview tiles, events-per-day chart, top values, live event feed, filters by event type / app / props), with Tracking (write keys + snippet) and Capture (auto-capture toggle: mode / topic patterns / sample rate) tabs. Write keys are write-only + project-bound; the platform API key never touches the browser.
apps.author: Apteva
